lessons.title: A Picnic by the River
lessons.audioFileName: Unit 1- A picnic by the river.mp3
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 1- A picnic by the river.mp3

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: This is a good spot. Let's stop and have our picnic next to the river.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Good idea. Walking always makes me hungry. I'm ready for lunch.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: We can sit here on the grass. Oh no! Someone forgot to throw these empty paper bags away. There is litter everywhere!

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Why do people always leave litter around? It's not a nice thing to do. It spoils other people's picnics.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I think they are lazy. Or maybe they just don't care. Look, there are some empty cans and glass bottles under that tree, too.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: People should clean up before they leave, and not leave litter lying around.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: That's right. Well, after our picnic, let's pick up all the litter we can and take it out of here.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: OK! And next week, let's come back with friends and pick up some more.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Good idea!

lessons.title: Let's Recycle!
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 2- Let's recycle.mp3

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Hi, Jane! Have you heard about the new laws to help people recycle?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I heard about them on the news last night. I don't think I like them.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: The government wants to keep the environment clean by recycling paper, metal, and glass instead of throwing these things away.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: But who wants to pay an extra 50 cents each time you buy a cup of coffee? That's a lot of money!

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: 50 cents? It's only five cents extra for a paper cup.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I thought it was 50 cents!

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: No, it's only five cents. Don't worry. And you can get your money back when you return the cup.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: That's fair. Well, maybe the government is right, after all. I'll return all the paper coffee cups I use from now on.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Good! We all need to recycle. It helps to keep the environment clean.

lessons.title: Growing Roses
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 3- Growing roses.mp3

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Excuse me, ma'am. I have a problem with my rose bush. It used to produce a lot of pink roses. But now it doesn't produce any flowers at all.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I see. That does seem like a problem. Do the leaves on the plant look healthy?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Not really. The leaves used to be very green. Now, most of them have turned brown.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Well, I think your rose bush needs some fertilizer.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: OK. What sort of fertilizer do you think I should use?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: This liquid fertilizer is very good. It will help make your rose leaves green again. Then the plant should produce roses quite soon. The fertilizer costs about ten dollars.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: How long will it take for my rose bush to recover?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: About two weeks, I think.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Great. I'll take it. Thank you so much for your help.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: You're welcome!

lessons.title: Bird Watching
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 4- Bird watching.mp3

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I want to go bird watching tomorrow. Do you know a good area for birds?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: There is a quiet park near here. There are always many beautiful birds there.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Will I be able to see different types of birds in this area?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Yes, I think so. If you use binoculars, you can see the birds, even if they are far away.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Great! I have a book about all the different types of birds.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: It seems as if you really like bird watching.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, I do! Would you like to come with me tomorrow?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: No, thank you. I think bird watching is boring.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's not true! Birds are very interesting. Some birds have colorful feathers. Some birds sing beautiful songs. Some birds make special nests to lay eggs in.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Really? Maybe I will go bird watching one day after all!

lessons.title: Trees in the Forest
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 5- Trees in the forest.mp3

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: There are many forests in North America. There are many trees in these forests. Some of these trees are more than two hundred feet tall. Some are over five hundred years old. Several kinds of trees grow in these forests. Fir, cedar, and pine are three. These trees grow in different areas. Some grow in forests. Some grow on the mountains. People who lived in this place long ago used these trees to make things out of wood. Many of these trees are now in special areas. These areas are called forest reserves or national parks. Some parks charge a small entrance fee. Visitors must pay the fee to enter the parks. Then they can walk among the beautiful old trees. They must take care not to damage the trees. We should all take care of forests.

lessons.title: An Easy Way to Shop
lessons.audioFileName: Unit 6 An Easy Way to Shop.mp3
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 6 An Easy Way to Shop.mp3

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Hey, Steve. Look at my new MP3 player!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wow! It looks cool! Where did you buy it?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: I bought it online at an electronics website.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'm not very good at using a computer. Is it hard to buy things online?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: It's really easy. All you do is go to the website, and choose the item you want to look at. There are so many items to choose from on the website! After you choose what you want to buy, you click on the "check out" button.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That does seem easy!

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Yes, it is. It only takes about a week for your item to come. Of course, if you are in a hurry, you can pay more to get it sent faster.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Do you pay for the item when it comes?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: No, you have to pay for it online with a credit card.

lessons.title: Cell Phone Messages
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 7 Cell Phone Messages.mp3

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I need to check my messages.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: How are you going to do that? We are in the middle of the freeway!

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I'm going to use my cell phone. Haven't you ever done that?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: No. I just use my cell phone to talk to other people.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Now you can also use a cell phone to send and receive short text messages. It's very useful.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: How do you send a message that way?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I just use the keys on the phone to type a short message. Then I press the "send" button. It's cheaper than making a phone call.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: That's a great idea! You can save both time and money that way.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Right. All my friends usually send me text messages now.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Thanks for telling me about this. I'll have to try it!

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: You're welcome. I think you'll find it useful.

lessons.title: Bubbles in Boiling Water
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 8 Bubbles in Boiling Water.mp3

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Where do the bubbles come from when you boil water? Water is a liquid. When it is heated, it moves around faster and faster. When it starts to boil, the liquid turns into a gas. This gas is called water vapor. This gas is lighter than the water around it. It rises to the top. Then it disappears into the air. As the water gets hotter and hotter, it starts turning into gas very quickly. A lot of bubbles form at the same time. All these bubbles try to escape at once. The bubbles push the water out of the way and "jump" out. This is what we call "boiling water." More and more water turns into gas. More of it disappears into the air. After a while, every drop of the water will be gone. Try it and see!

lessons.title: The Blue Sky
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 9 The Blue Sky.mp3

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Joe asked me something about science just now. But I didn't know the answer.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: I'm good at science. Ask me.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: OK. Why is the sky blue?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: I'll explain it in a simple way. Light comes through the air from the sun in waves.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The light is in many colors, right?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Right. Blue light waves are smaller than air molecules. They sometimes get absorbed by these molecules.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: OK. What happens then?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Then the blue light waves scatter in many directions. Your eyes see this blue light from above you, after it leaves the air molecules.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So that is what makes the sky blue! What happens to the other colors?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: They reflect off the things that they hit. Your shirt is red because our eyes see the red light reflected from it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Now I understand why the sky is blue!

lessons.title: A New Camera
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 10 A New Camera.mp3

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I just bought a digital camera!

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: What is wrong with your old camera?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Nothing. I bought this one because I want to store my pictures on my computer.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I can also delete pictures that are not very good. I don't have to print them.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I like to print all my photos. That's why I like the old cameras.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Oh, you can print digital photos, too. Many shops will print them for you.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Really?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Yes. You can even buy a good printer and do it from home.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: That seems easy! How do you store these digital pictures?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: You can store the pictures on your computer. But you might run out of space. I save all the pictures I like on compact discs. You can store more than seven hundred photos on one CD!

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Great! Maybe I should get a digital camera, too. Art and Culture

lessons.title: Gold
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 11 Gold.mp3

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Gold has been a part of many cultures for hundreds of years. People made coins and jewelry with gold. Gold is a soft metal. It is easy to shape into sheets, long wires, or rings. People sometimes mix gold with other metals. This makes the gold harder. Then it can be made into beautiful jewelry. Why do we value gold so much? It has a special color. No other metal is a bright yellow. We also value gold because it is rare. A rare thing is hard to find. Even after hundreds of years, gold is still a precious metal now. It is still valued for its beauty. It is still rare. Today, banks store gold in the form of bars. Its value is more than $600 per ounce. Gold is more useful now than ever before.

lessons.title: The Summer Music Festival
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 12 The Summer Music Festival.mp3

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Have you heard about the music festival next summer? I read that it is going to have about 20 different bands playing in it.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I think I did hear someone talking about it. Are you planning on going?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I'll go if I can get tickets. I heard that people are going to line up overnight to get tickets. I might line up overnight, too.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I don't think I want to line up all night long!

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Well, I'm going to do it. I think it is going to be a great music festival that I won't want to miss.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Maybe. Do you know how much the tickets are going to cost?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I'm not sure, but I think each ticket will be about $75.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: That's a lot of money! I don't think I want to spend that much on a ticket. Good luck, anyway!

lessons.title: The School Play
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 13 The School Play.mp3

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Are you going to the school play on Saturday night?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: The school play? I didn't know there was going to be a play on Saturday night.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, I heard about it in English class yesterday. I think it will be really good.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Who told you about it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ms. Martin, our English teacher, told us all about it. This is the drama club's first play of the year.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: What is the play about? I hope it's nothing boring.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Can you guess what it is?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Oh, come on, tell me please!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's The Sound of Music.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Really? I watched The Sound of Music on TV last month! It's very good! Are you sure?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Of course I'm sure, that's what Ms. Martin said. Would you like to watch the play with me on Saturday night?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: That would be great! Let's go early so we get good seats!

lessons.title: Ballet Class
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 14 Ballet Class.mp3

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Hi Cindy, where are you going?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Good afternoon, Mrs. White, I'm going to ballet class.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Ballet class? I didn't know you were studying ballet. How long have you been studying ballet?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Today is my first day, and I don't want to go. My mom and dad want me to learn ballet. I'm not sure I want to learn how to dance.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I used to learn ballet too, when I was your age. Now I teach ballet in a dance school.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Oh, I didn't know that! Where do you teach your classes?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Down the street at Easy Steps Dance Academy. Ballet is fun to learn, and it's a very graceful dance. You'll need to learn the steps and practice a lot of course, but I think you'll enjoy it.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: I hope so!

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Well, go and have some fun dancing!

lessons.title: Monet's Garden
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 15 Monet’s Garden.mp3

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Claude Monet was a great artist. He was the first of a group of artists called the Impressionists. This group of artists thought about how things in the world made them feel. They tried to show this in their work. This way of painting shows how light can change shapes and colors. Monet did a lot of his work outdoors. He wanted to show how daylight made things look. Many of his paintings are of gardens. He liked to paint flowers and trees. He loved to paint in his own garden. His garden was in a village. He lived there for many years. Today, many visitors come each year to this garden. They come from all over the world. Most of them are art lovers or artists. They come to see the place that Monet loved so much. Leisure and Entertainment

lessons.title: A Haunted House
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 16 A Haunted House.mp3

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Oh no, it's raining! I wanted to go to the beach today.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Well, I'm visiting a haunted house this afternoon. You can come with me if you like.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: A haunted house? What is it like?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's really dark, with lots of old furniture and pictures on the walls. It's called a haunted house because it's full of ghosts!

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: You're joking, right? I don't believe in ghosts! Where is the haunted house?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The house is in the old forest.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Oh! Are you really sure you want to go?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What's wrong? I thought you didn't believe in ghosts!

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Well, I don't really believe in ghosts, but . . .

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's OK, I don't believe in ghosts, either! I was only joking. The old house isn't really haunted; it's just a very old, empty house.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Whew, I'm glad to hear that! Sure, I'll come with you!

lessons.title: A Big Screen TV
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 17 A Big Screen TV.mp3

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I'm thinking about buying a big screen TV.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Wow! I've seen those in the store. They cost a lot of money. Can you afford to buy one?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: They do cost a lot of money. But I really enjoy watching TV. I think it's much more fun to watch TV shows on a big screen.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I've never watched TV on a big screen. Do you think the quality of the picture is good?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Yes, the quality is great. When you watch soccer games, you feel like you are right there on the field!

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: When you buy the TV, can I come over to your house? Then, I can enjoy watching TV on the big screen with you!

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I have to save some money to buy the TV first. It will be a few months before I can afford to buy it!

lessons.title: He's Famous!
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 18 He’s Famous!.mp3

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Are you going to the new Tim Cross movie tonight?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: I don't know. It looks kind of boring.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Really? I think it looks quite interesting. Besides, Tim Cross is a famous actor.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: He may be famous, but I don't think he's a very good actor. He always acts in the same sort of movie. He never does anything different.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Well, at least you think he's good looking, right?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: No, not really. He always looks so sleepy.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: But most girls think he's handsome. Maybe that's why he is so famous.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: None of my friends think he is good looking at all. I used to like him a few years ago, but now I think he's not handsome at all.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hey! I just got a haircut to try to look more like him!

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Well, that explains why I don't like your new haircut!

lessons.title: A Housewarming Party
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 19 A Housewarming Party.mp3

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Hi, Steve! Thanks for coming to my housewarming party.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Hello, Sue! Thanks for inviting me to see your lovely new home. It's beautiful!

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Thank you. I'm glad you like it.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Did you decorate your house all by yourself?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Yes, I did. I traveled around Europe last year. I got some beautiful furniture for my house there.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Do you plan to go on a new trip this summer?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Yes, I am planning to visit China.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: That's great! How long will you be there?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I will be there for a month.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: You can find some beautiful things in China for your new house. You should go shopping while you are there.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Of course! It will be fun to go shopping there. By the way, please help yourself to the refreshments.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Thanks. The food looks delicious!

lessons.title: Making Music
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 20 Making Music.mp3

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Do you like to listen to music? Music is made up of sound. People all over the world like music. People have liked it for hundreds of years. People who write music are called composers. Most of the time, a composer does not sing or play his own music. He writes it all down in the form of notes. Those who know how to read music can understand these notes. This is how people can sing the song or play it. Lots of people like to play music. Music can be played on instruments. There are many types of musical instruments. Some of these are the piano, the violin, and the drum. People can make music as a group. A choir is a group of people who sing. An orchestra is a group of people who play musical instruments. School and Family

lessons.title: Where Is Your Homework?
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 21 Where Is Your Homework.mp3

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Did you finish your homework for English class?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Homework? There wasn't any homework.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: We had to finish reading a book and then write a 200-word essay on it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I don't think Ms. Jones gave us any homework. I always write what I have to do in my notebook. Did she really tell us to write an essay?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Yes. Look, here's my essay. See?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh no! What am I going to do? We've only got 10 minutes before class starts.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: I don't know. Maybe Ms. Jones will let you hand it in tomorrow.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hey, let me copy your essay. I'll change a few words. Ms. Jones will never know.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: No, I'm sorry. That's not the right thing to do.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh, come on! I thought you were my friend.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: I am your friend. That's why I'm not letting you copy my work!

lessons.title: After School Activities
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 22 After School Activities.mp3

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Will you play any sports this school year?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: I want to play hockey. But I'm not sure if I will have enough time.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'm on the school soccer team. I'm also going to take up swimming.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: You're going to be on the soccer team and swim, too?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: That seems like a lot. You will be very busy! Do you think you will have any free time?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I will play soccer with my school team during the week. I will go swimming during the weekend.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: When will you have time to do your homework? And when will you study?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I do my homework after school every day. I study every weekend. My mother won't let me play sports until I have done all my work.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Well, I hope you find enough time for both schoolwork and sports. Good luck!

lessons.title: Arts and Crafts Class
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 23 Arts and Crafts Class.mp3

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Hi, Mom, I'm back from arts and crafts class. Look at what I'm wearing.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Well, you're wearing a blue T-shirt and jeans.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Sure, but what else am I wearing?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Oh, those earrings are very pretty! Is that what you're learning to make this week in arts and crafts class?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Yes, we're learning to make jewelry from beads this week. The beads come in different colors and shapes. First, we decide what sort of jewelry we want to make. Then, we choose the beads we want, and string them on transparent plastic wire.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: That sounds like a lot of fun!

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Yeah! Tom made a bead necklace for his sister, and I made some earrings. Guess what, Mom? I made a pair of earrings for you, too!

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Oh, these are very pretty! Thank you very much.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Next week, I'm going to make a necklace.

lessons.title: Grandfather's Birthday
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 24 Grandfather’s Birthday.mp3

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hi, Mom! Guess what? We got our English test back today. I got the highest score in my class!

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Oh, Billy, I'm glad you did so well! You worked hard for that test.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Thanks, Mom. I'm hungry. What's for dinner?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: We're going to your aunt's place for dinner tonight. It's your grandfather's birthday today, remember?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh no, I forgot! I haven't got a birthday gift for Grandpa!

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Don't worry. I bought a gift for him yesterday from the three of us. Anyway, your English test score is a good gift for your grandfather. The whole family will be at the party tonight. All your aunts, uncles, and cousins are coming.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I haven't seen the whole family in a long time.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Well, you'll see them tonight. Now, hurry up and get ready.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: OK. When are we leaving?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: When your father gets home from work.

lessons.title: The Lesson
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 25 The Lesson.mp3

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: There was once a man who lived with his two sons. The two sons were always fighting with each other. One day, the man decided to teach his sons a lesson. The man gave his younger son two large sticks. He told the boy to break them. The boy tried hard, but he could not break the sticks. The older son also could not break the sticks. At last, the man gave only one stick to each son. He said, "Break them." Each son broke his stick easily. The man said, "You are like these sticks. If you work together, no one can break you. But if you fight with each other all the time, one day, someone will break both of you." After that lesson, the sons stopped fighting. They started to work together. People and Work

lessons.title: A Problem at the Office
lessons.audioFileName: Unit 26 A Problem at the Office.mp3
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 26 A Problem at the Office.mp3

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I had a big problem at the office today!

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: What happened?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I could not use my computer all day!

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Was it because of a virus?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Yes. I opened a file that had a virus.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Oh no! You must be careful when you open files in your email. A virus can make your whole computer crash.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: It was an accident! I didn't know the file had a virus. I'll be more careful next time.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: What did you do next?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I asked a computer repairman to come to the office. He worked all day to repair my computer. But the real problem is that I may have lost some of my work.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Don't worry. Your work is probably still on your computer. I can help you get it back. Next time, make sure you have back-up files. Just in case it happens again!

lessons.title: My Future Job
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 27 My Future Job.mp3

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: What do you want to be when you grow up, Mark?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I want to be a teacher. I think I would like to help children learn.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Well, you know, teachers work very hard, and they are not paid much money.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I don't care about money. Teaching is an important job.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: What subject do you want to teach?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I want to teach mathematics, like Ms. Kim. She makes learning fun. I didn't know that I would like math so much until I joined her class. Now, mathematics is my favorite subject.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: If you want to teach math, you'll have to work hard and learn it well.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No problem! I got an A on the mathematics examination last week. With good teachers like Ms. Kim, learning is easy.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: I want to be a teacher, too. But I want to teach English, not math!

lessons.title: Shopping
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 28 Shopping.mp3

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: We are having a summer sale. Everything is 50% off the normal price.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Really? Everything?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Yes. Everything is on sale, including sunglasses, hats, and bags. All the summer clothes are on sale, too.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I do need some new sunglasses. I lost mine when I went to the beach this summer. Oh, these are really nice. What is the price of these? There is no price tag on them.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Well, sir, there's no price tag on those sunglasses because they are mine!

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Really? I would like to get a pair of sunglasses just like these. Where did you get them?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Actually, I got them for $15 at Super Glasses.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: There is a Super Glasses store in this mall, isn't there?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Yes, but let me show you the sunglasses we have on sale.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: No, thanks. I think I'll just go to Super Glasses!

lessons.title: A Part-time Job
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 29 A Part-time Job.mp3

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I want to find a part-time job. Do you have any ideas about where I should look for work?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Have you looked in the newspaper? There are lots of job advertisements in the newspaper.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, I have. But there were no jobs I was interested in.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Did you search on the Internet? Many companies put job advertisements on the Internet.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No, I haven't looked on the Internet. I don't know what I should search for.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: There are many websites that have job postings that you could look at. You could also search for the type of job you are interested in.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: OK. Thanks for telling me what I need to do. I'll start my Internet search right now.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I have a list of some websites. You could start looking at those first. That might save you some time.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That would be very useful. Thanks!

lessons.title: Teamwork
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 30 Teamwork.mp3

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: When people work together as a team, they can achieve a lot. You can easily get things done when you share the work. We practice teamwork in my family. Both my parents have jobs. My father is a doctor. My mother is a teacher. Both of them work long hours all week. My brother is a student at college. I am a student in school. We all have very busy lives. So, when it comes to household chores, we all work together to get them done. Each of us has different chores. My parents take turns to cook. My father takes out the trash. My mother does the laundry. My brother washes the dishes. I sweep the floor. We share the chores and work together. Everything gets done fast. People should practice working as a team. Teamwork works! Sports and Health

lessons.title: The Marathon
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 31 The Marathon.mp3

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Did you watch the Boston marathon?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Yes, I went to Boston to see it.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: You were in Boston for the marathon?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: That's right. My friend is a runner, so I went there to watch her run. We traveled to Boston together.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: You are so lucky! Which part of the marathon did you see?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I watched the entire race, from start to finish.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I don't know how the runners can finish the whole race! It's so long and difficult! I could never do something like that.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I tried to run a marathon once. It was really difficult. I just can't run like my friend can.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Yes, running a marathon is not an easy thing to do. By the way, how did your friend do in the race?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: She did quite well! She was not the fastest runner, but she was in the top 50.

lessons.title: Racquetball
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 32 Racquetball.mp3

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Racquetball is a popular sport. It was first played in the US. This game started just a little more than 50 years ago. That makes it quite a new sport. Other racket sports like tennis and squash have been played for a long time. Racquetball rules are a mix of rules from both handball and squash. A short racket is used to play this game. This game became popular almost at once when it first came out. More and more people wanted to play it. Clubs began to build racquetball courts. They built these courts for players of this new sport. People of all ages can play this game. But most players today are young people. Most of them are between the ages of 12 and 34. Racquetball is now a famous sport. It is played all over the world.

lessons.title: Summer Sports
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 33 Summer Sports.mp3

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hi, Alice. What have you been doing? You look tired.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: I stayed up late last night to watch the Olympics. We won a gold medal for men's basketball. We also won the silver medal for women's tennis.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's great! What about gymnastics?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: The men's team didn't do so well. But the women's team won the silver medal.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I haven't had much time to watch, but I saw the opening ceremony.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: What have you been doing this summer?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I've been playing baseball and taking swimming lessons.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: I like to watch baseball. Maybe I can come and watch your team play some time. When do you usually play?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We have a game this weekend. Why don't you come and watch us play in the park?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Sure! Just let me know what time the game starts. See you later.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Bye!

lessons.title: Inline Skating
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 34 Inline Skating.mp3

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh! My legs are so sore!

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Really? What did you do during the weekend?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I went inline skating with my friends at the park.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Did you have fun?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, I did. But it was also my first time, so it was really difficult. I was scared that I would fall down. After a short time, my muscles were really tired.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Next time will be easier. You just need more practice.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What about you? What did you do during the weekend?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Actually, I also went inline skating. I go every weekend with my father. We usually skate about 20 kilometers each time.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wow! How can you skate so far? Your muscles must be really strong.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: I've been skating for three years now. You could skate that far, too. You just need to build up your muscles. Let's go skating together next weekend.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: OK!

lessons.title: The Olympics
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 35 The Olympics.mp3

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: The Olympic Games are a famous world sports event. These games are held once in four years. There are summer games and winter games. People come from countries all over the world to compete in the games. These games started a long time ago in Greece. In those days, only men took part in them. There were only a few sports events. Now, women take part in the Olympic Games, too. There are team sports, like basketball. There are martial arts, like judo. More and more types of sports are in the games each time they are held. It is very hard to win a medal at these games. Only world champions take part in the Olympics. Those who compete must work hard for years. Their bodies must be very fit. They must be the best to win medals in these games.

lessons.title: A Bicycle Trip
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 36 A Bicycle Trip.mp3

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I'm planning to go on a bicycle trip around Europe.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Why do you want to go on a bicycle trip?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: It is an environmentally friendly way to travel.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: What do you have to do in order to go on a bicycle trip?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Before the trip, I'll need to ride my bicycle a lot. That will make me fit and strong. I also need to get some equipment.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: What kind of equipment will you need?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I need road maps of the countries I am going to visit. I also need strong bags to carry clothes and food. I need to carry all these things on my bicycle.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Are you traveling with another person?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Yes, I am going with a friend of mine. He likes bicycle trips.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I wish I could go on a bicycle trip, too! Well, don't get too many flat tires!

lessons.title: Driving Down South
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 37 Driving Down South.mp3

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Isn't it great that there aren't any classes on Monday? We have a three-day weekend!

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: That's right! Do you have any special plans?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: My family is taking a trip to Las Cruces. I'm really looking forward to it. Have you ever been there?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: No, but I've heard about it. Is it nice?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, there are so many things to see. The city is famous for its nuts.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: What kind of nuts?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Pecans. There are many pecan trees growing in and around the city.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: I like pecans. How far away is Las Cruces from here?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It only takes about four hours by car if you use the freeway and drive directly south.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: That certainly makes for an easy trip. When are you leaving?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We're going on Saturday morning. We'll be back on Monday evening.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Have a nice time! Bring me some pecans!

lessons.title: The Travel Agent
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 38 The Travel Agent.mp3

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I want to go on a trip to China.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: How long do you want to stay?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Four or five days.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: We have a very good package tour that is for four days and three nights.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: OK. What can you tell me about it?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Well, you'll fly directly to Beijing. Your tour guide will meet you at the airport and take you to your hotel. Over the four days, you will do a lot of sightseeing. You will see many famous landmarks, like the Summer Palace, the Forbidden City, and the Great Wall of China.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: That sounds great! What sort of transport will we use to get from one place to another?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: You will take a bus with your tour group.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: OK. Can I book this package tour now? There will be five of us going on this trip.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Sure!

lessons.title: Taking the Train
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 39 Taking the Train.mp3

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: You're so lucky, Marian. You're leaving for Hawaii in five hours! I never travel because I hate flying in airplanes. I don't like buses, either.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: That doesn't matter, Dean. There are other ways to get around. You should take the train somewhere.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: That's true. It's been a long time since I last traveled. I've always wanted to take a long train trip.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: What's stopping you? Go to the travel agent now and ask about train trips!

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: What do you think the fares are like?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I'm not sure what train fares are like now. I think it depends on your destination. That's a question you'll have to ask a travel agent.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Can you suggest a good person to talk to?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: My travel agent is always very helpful. Here is his phone number.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Thanks! I'll call him right now. Where's the phone?

lessons.title: Go on a Cruise!
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 1/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 40 Go on a Cruise!.mp3

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Are you sick of long road trips in a car? Do you find long trips in an airplane boring? Do you want to travel in a special way? You should take a cruise to all the places you would like to see! Go by cruise ship to the northeast part of the US! Go late in the year. Then, you can enjoy the colors of the autumn leaves on the trees. It is a beautiful sight. Do you like to look at man-made wonders? Go on a cruise to the Panama Canal! Do you want to see icebergs? Do you want to look at seals and whales? Go on a cruise to Alaska! Wherever you may choose to go, a cruise is a great way to travel. Book a trip on a cruise ship today! You will love it!

lessons.title: Antarctica
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 1 Antarctica.mp3

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Antarctica is another name for the South Pole. It is also a continent. A long time ago, the South Pole was close to the equator. That was 500 million years ago. It was once joined to Australia. Then, all the land on Earth started to move. Antarctica moved away from Australia and went south. Dinosaur bones were once found at the South Pole. Do you know why? Dinosaurs lived there millions of years ago. This was before it moved away from the equator. About 98% of this continent is frozen. The rest is made up of rock. The South Pole has 87% of the world's ice. But did you know that it gets very little snow? Only about two inches of snow falls each year. How many people live on your continent? No one lives in the South Pole. Only animals, like penguins, live there. Scientists and tourists visit there, but they don't stay long. Do you want to visit Antarctica? It is the coldest, driest place on Earth!

lessons.title: A Hiking Trip
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 2 A Hiking Trip.mp3

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Hi, Anne! Did you sign up for the trip on Saturday?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: What trip is that? I didn't know there was a trip on Saturday.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: The hiking club is going to Bear Mountain. The bus drops us off at the bottom, and we're going to hike until we get to a cabin halfway up the mountain.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: That sounds really great! Where can I sign up?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Go and see Jennifer. She'll help you sign up.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: What activity will we do when we get to the cabin on the mountain?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Well, it takes seven hours to hike to the cabin, so it will be late by the time we arrive. After we unpack, we'll start a campfire. Then we can sing, eat, and tell stories around the fire. The following day we'll leave at dawn and hike to the top of the mountain. After we take pictures, we'll hike back down. If we have time, we might go swimming in the lake on the mountain!

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Those sound like really fun activities, and I can't wait to go!

lessons.title: Save the Turtles
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 3 Save the Turtles.mp3

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Have you heard about the plan to save turtles in Mexico?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: No. What is the story?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Turtles are in danger of becoming extinct around the world. Every year, thousands of turtles lay eggs on the beach. After the turtles lay their eggs in the sand, people come along and take them.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I suppose the people like eating turtle eggs.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Exactly. Turtles are beginning to stay away from certain places, now. There are fewer and fewer of them left. There is a new project in Mexico to save these eggs. Then turtles will not become extinct. I think it's a very good project.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Is there anything we can do to help?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I'm going to call the Environmental Protection hotline. They might have some information about the project to help save turtles in Mexico.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: They might even have a brochure. Let's find the website on my computer. Oh, here it is. The address is www.envir o.com. There's plenty of information here.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Great! Let's see what we can do to help save turtles in Mexico.

lessons.title: Hiking in Iran
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 4 Hiking in Iran.mp3

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Most people think that the Middle East is only a desert. This is far from true. Last year, I went hiking in Iran. Iran has many mountains. You can find trees that lose their leaves in winter. If you're lucky, you may see a yellow deer or a brown bear, two species that live there. The air is fresh, and you can swim in clear, clean lakes. I definitely recommend it. There are so many birds to see. It is fun to go into the forest with binoculars to look at birds. Seeing the birds through binoculars makes them seem much nearer than they actually are. You can write down all of the species that you see. You should learn about their calls first. That means the sounds that each bird makes. Sometimes it's hard to see the birds. However, you can identify them if you happen to hear them. I want to go back to Iran again someday. It's so beautiful that I want to see and explore much more of it!

lessons.title: Jane Goodall
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 5 Jane Goodall.mp3

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Jane Goodall went to Africa when she was 26 years old. She went there to research chimpanzees. At that time, no other women scientists worked there alone. At first, Jane studied the chimps from far away. The chimps were afraid of her. They ran away if she came close to them. After some time, the chimps saw that she was not going to hurt them. They let her walk near them. Soon, she was living among them. She wanted to learn more and more about them. Jane did a lot of research on chimps. She discovered many new things about them. She learned that each chimp has its own personality. She saw that they have feelings. Jane discovered that chimps have very close families. Mothers and fathers take good care of baby chimps. An adult female chimp will sometimes adopt an orphan. In 1977, Jane started an institute to help protect animals. She wanted to help animals all around the world. Today, this institute runs programs in over 70 countries.

lessons.title: Flying Cars
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 6 Flying Cars.mp3

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Listen to this! This newspaper article says that some scientists are working on a new kind of airplane. People can use these "flying cars" for short trips.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: How interesting!

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: The article says the first flying car might be ready within the next few years.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: That's quite soon! How would this flying car work? Can anybody use one, or is it only for people who know how to fly airplanes?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: You don't need to be an airplane pilot to use a flying car. The article says there would be a computer inside the car that would know where you want to go. The driver does not need to control the car unless something goes wrong.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Does the article say how much a flying car would cost? It will probably cost too much money! We would not be able to afford one.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: True, but wouldn't it be nice to fly over traffic jams, instead of sitting in the middle of them?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Yes. But then we might end up with traffic jams in the sky!

lessons.title: The Perfect Gift
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 7 The Perfect Gift.mp3

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Hello, and welcome to Robuck's. How may I help you?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I would like to buy my wife a home appliance for her birthday.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: What sort of appliance are you looking for, sir?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I think a dishwasher might be the perfect gift because it will help with the housework.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Oh yes, dishwashers are very useful. This one here is our most popular model.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: How does it work?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: It's very simple. First, collect your dirty dishes and scrape off the leftover food into the garbage can. Then, rinse the dishes in the sink. Put glasses, cups, and cutlery on the top rack. Plates, bowls, and pots go face down on the bottom rack. Then, fill this compartment with detergent and close the door. Next, choose the wash cycle, and finally, press the start button. You'll have sparkling clean dishes in 45 minutes!

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: That sounds easy to use. I think my wife will really like it. How much does it cost?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: You're lucky, sir! It's on sale this week for $400.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Great, I'll take it!

lessons.title: Acupuncture
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 8 Acupuncture.mp3

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Acupuncture began in China thousands of years ago. It is a special way to treat sick people. There are many acupuncture spots on the human body. Small metal needles are put into spots on the body. Each spot is connected to a special body part or system. There are many spots for each part. An expert puts the needles into these spots in a person's body. These spots connect to the body system that has a problem. The needles do not go deep. People say that the needles do not hurt. We are not sure why acupuncture works. But studies have shown that it works very well. No one can explain why. Doctors think that it helps the nerves in the body. Some doctors use acupuncture to treat people who cannot take medicine. People in Asia have been using this special method for a long time. At first, people outside Asia did not trust this method. They did not think that it would help them. Now, it has become very popular around the world.

lessons.title: Albert Einstein
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 9 Albert Einstein.mp3

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Albert Einstein is famous around the world. He is famous for his work in science. Many people think that he was the greatest scientist of the 20 th century. Einstein was born in Germany in 1879. His interest in science began when he was very young. Someone gave him a compass in 1884. Young Einstein was interested in how it worked. He wanted to learn science. He wanted to become a scientist. Einstein tried to enter a top Swiss university. At first, he met with failure. He did not get a place. But Einstein did not give up easily. He applied again to the same university in the next year. This time he was successful. Einstein was a good student. He graduated from this famous university in 1896. As a scientist, Einstein did important work in the field of physics. His work was very good. He received the Nobel Prize for physics in 1921. In 1933, he went to live in the United States with his wife.

lessons.title: The Telescope
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 10 The Telescope.mp3

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Come and look at the telescope I got for my birthday.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's neat!

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Yeah, now we can look at the moon. Did you know that the moon is the Earth's only natural satellite?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No, I didn't know that. I thought the moon was a planet.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Well, a planet moves around the sun, but a satellite moves around a planet.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh, I see. Can you see other planets with your telescope?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Sure, I can see two planets close to Earth really well.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Which planet is closest to Earth?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Mars is the closest planet to Earth. Many scientists believe that Mars once had rivers and oceans just like Earth. Mars has two moons.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's cool! What is the other planet near Earth?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: The other planet near Earth is Venus, but Venus has no moons.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Do you think people will ever be able to visit Mars or Venus?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Maybe someday people will be able to visit Mars, but not Venus because it's too hot.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Well, at least we can see them with your new telescope! Art and Culture

lessons.title: The Mona Lisa
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 11 The Mona Lisa.mp3

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: What are you looking at, Billy?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: This is a copy of my favorite painting. It's the Mona Lisaby Leonardo da Vinci.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Why is that your favorite painting?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Well, there are a few things that make the Mona Lisa great. First, she has no eyebrows. Second, she has a really beautiful smile. Most of all, I like the soft colors of the painting. Have you seen the Mona Lisa before? It is a very famous painting!

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Of course! I've seen the painting a few times before. But I never noticed that her eyebrows are missing. I wonder why she has no eyebrows. Do you know why?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: At the time da Vinci painted it, it was fashionable for young Italian girls to shave off their eyebrows. Every girl wanted to be fashionable.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Wow! That's really interesting! In what year was the Mona Lisa painted?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I think it was painted sometime between 1503 and 1505.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: I wonder what a modern Mona Lisa would look like.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: She might have purple hair!

lessons.title: Bang Yi
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 12 Bang Yi.mp3

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Once upon a time, there was a poor, kind man named Bang Yi. He had a rich but greedy brother. One day, Bang Yi asked his brother to give him some grain seeds to grow. His greedy brother gave Bang Yi some poisoned seeds. Only one plant grew from the poisoned seeds, but Bang Yi was very happy. He took good care of the plant. Then, one afternoon, a bird came and stole the plant. Bang Yi chased the bird into the forest. In the forest, he saw two monsters using a magic stick to turn rocks into food. Bang Yi hid behind a big rock and watched the monsters. The monsters ate a lot of food. Soon, they became very sleepy. When the monsters had fallen asleep, Bang Yi took their magic stick. He became very rich! Bang Yi's greedy brother went to the forest to find a magic stick for himself. The angry monsters saw him. They chased him deep into the forest. The greedy brother was never seen again.

lessons.title: Friendship Day
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 13 Friendship Day.mp3

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Friends are an important part of our lives. They help us in many ways. Do you tell your friends that you are glad they are your friends? Everyone should tell their friends that they are special. Did you know that there is now a special day just for friends? This day is called National Friendship Day. The first Sunday in August was chosen to be National Friendship Day in 1935. This holiday is not as big as Christmas or New Year's Day. However, it is still a special day. People are usually too busy to visit their friends often. But this day is different. On this day, people take time to tell their friends how much they care. They write cards or send emails to their friends. They may also call their friends, no matter how busy they are. People hug their friends or spend time with them. There are many ways to show you care. You need not wait for a special day. Call your friends right now!

lessons.title: An Outdoor Exhibit
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 14 An Outdoor Exhibit.mp3

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Do you like photographs?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: What kind of photos?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Photos of plants and animals, for example. Or mountains and oceans.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: The sort of photographs a nature magazine would publish.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: That's right.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Of course! I love nature photos. They are very beautiful.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Some of them are very colorful.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Yes. Most nature photos are so interesting. Sometimes, I buy nature magazines just for the photos.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Me, too. I like taking nature photos with my camera. But they are not very good.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: My photos are not good, either. Famous nature magazines only publish very good photos.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: That's true. People must be very talented to get their photos published.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Yeah. Why are we suddenly talking about photographs? Is there an exhibit somewhere?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: How did you guess? There is an outdoor exhibit going on right now.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Really?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Yes. Nature photographs from all over the world are on display.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: That sounds great! I would love to see it.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Me, too. Would you like to go with me?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Sure. How about Sunday morning?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: OK! It will be fun to see all those photos!

lessons.title: People Are Different!
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 15 People Are Different!.mp3

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: There are more than six billion human beings in the world. Each one is different from all the others. No two people look exactly alike. People from one country may look the same in general. But they are not totally alike. Most people in Vietnam have straight black hair and black eyes. But they all look different. People in America have straight hair, curly hair, or wavy hair. Their hair may be black, brown, yellow, or red. Some people have brown or gray eyes. Some have blue or green eyes. Even people in the same family look different from each other! We all think differently. We all like different things. We like different kinds of food and different kinds of music. We also like different styles of clothing. Wherever you are, you are different from everyone else. Nobody else looks just like you. Nobody has your thoughts or your talents. There are more than six billion people on Earth, but none of them are exactly like you. You are one of a kind! Leisure and Entertainment

lessons.title: Karaoke
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 16 Karaoke.mp3

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: It's nice to see you, Karen. How have you been?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I've been very well, thank you. How are you, Dan?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I'm fine, thanks. I went to the movies Saturday night. I wanted to invite you, but you weren't home.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: That's right, I went karaoke singing with some friends on Saturday night.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Really? I've never sung karaoke. What's it like?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I had never gone karaoke singing before either, but I had a great time. My friends were experienced karaoke singers, so they showed me what to do.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Did you have to sing in front of a lot of strangers?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: No, the place we went to rented out small private rooms. Nobody else could hear us. They even gave us free sodas!

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Cool! What kind of music did they have?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: They had hundreds of different songs to choose from. They had both new songs and old songs. They had songs in English and songs in several other languages, too. It was really fun!

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I think I'll go karaoke singing next weekend!

lessons.title: Watching TV
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 17 Watching TV.mp3

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Did you watch the latest episode of that new reality show last night?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: There are so many of those reality shows these days. Which one are you talking about?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: It's called "Good Fences," and it's all about neighbors. This reality show is the only one I like, because you're right, the others are just silly.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I never watch reality shows at all. I prefer to watch shows that teach me about something, like science and nature programs, and travel shows.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Oh, I like travel shows, too. My favorite travel show is the one with that chef from England. He travels, cooks, and eats all the time!

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I like that one, too. He really makes me laugh. He has a good sense of humor.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Let's watch it together this week. It's on Thursday at eight o'clock, right?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: That's right, but where shall we watch it?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Well, I have a big-screen TV and a comfortable sofa.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: OK, we'll watch it at your place then, and I'll bring some snacks. See you then!

lessons.title: Have Some Fun!
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 18 Have Some Fun!.mp3

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: OK, great, we'll meet you in an hour. Bye.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Who was that on the phone, Jane?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: That was Amy. She wants to meet us in front of her apartment building in an hour.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Why are we meeting her there?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Because her apartment is close to the bus stop. We're going to go downtown and watch a movie, so hurry up and get ready.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Oh, I honestly don't think I should watch a movie tonight. I'm studying for an important test on Tuesday, so I really don't have time to have fun!

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: You have been studying for several days, Joe. You don't need to study anymore. You need to have some fun because you're too tired to study, anyway.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I don't know, maybe you're right. Is it just Amy and us going?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Lily is coming along, too.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Really? I need time to take a shower and get dressed!

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Don't worry, you have time.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: It will be fun to see Lily and fun to watch a movie together.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I told you so!

lessons.title: Tickets to the Game
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 19 Tickets to the Game.mp3

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: You won't believe this, but I have some great news! I've got two tickets to the baseball game next Saturday.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Did I hear you correctly? You have two tickets to the baseball game? How did you get those? I thought it was impossible to get tickets because they were all sold out last month!

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: It was easy, actually. My colleague and her husband have to go to London that week, so they'll miss the game. They offered me their tickets, and of course I was happy to accept.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: You're so lucky! Who are you going to take with you?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I was thinking that maybe you would like to go. Otherwise, I might take my brother instead.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Don't do that, I would love to watch the game with you!

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I was just joking. I know you really want to go. Where shall we meet on Saturday?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Well, the game starts at nine o'clock in the morning, right?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Yes, shall we meet here at 8:30 a.m. on Saturday?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Good idea. I can't wait!

lessons.title: Wonder Woman
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 20 Wonder Woman.mp3

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Comic book heroes have been popular for many years. One hero has the strength of one hundred men. This hero also has the speed of lightning. This hero cannot be killed. If you think this hero is Superman, you are wrong! This hero is Wonder Woman! Aman called William Marston created Wonder Woman in 1941. He was a graduate of Harvard University. He used a false name on his comics. He did not want his colleagues to know that he wrote comics. The false name was Charles Moulton. Mr. Marston wanted to make a strong female hero for little girls. Of course, he hoped that little boys would like Wonder Woman, too. Wonder Woman was not very popular at first. Then, World War II began in 1941. Wonder Woman became a role model for children around the world. She was both strong and beautiful. She always tried to do what was right. Today, she is still one of the most popular heroes of all time. School and Family

lessons.title: Blood Types
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 21 Blood Types.mp3

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Thanks for meeting with me today, Professor. I don't understand last week's lecture on blood types. Could you please explain it to me?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: No problem, Angela. First, let's see what you do understand. Can you tell me about blood types?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: There are four types of blood: A, B, AB, and O.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Good! How is your blood type determined?

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: You get your blood type from both your parents. Your blood type is a combination of genes from your father and your mother.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: That's right.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Before the lecture, I always thought that all blood was the same. Why can't two different blood types mix?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: In some ways, every person's blood is the same. But it is very dangerous to mix two different blood types. Your blood cells may begin to stick together. If you are given the wrong type of blood in a hospital, you could die.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Isee. So, that's why blood types must be matched in the hospital. And this must be done before blood is given to anyone.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Exactly!

lessons.title: The Car Ride
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 22 The Car Ride.mp3

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mom, Danielle's on my side of the car again. Tell her to move over!

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Listen, both of you, I've had enough of your nonsense. Sit still, be quiet, and enjoy the scenery!

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Mom, is Toronto still far away?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: It's going to take a long time to get there, so read your book.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: I don't like to read in the car because it gives me a headache. Can we put a CD in?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I suppose so, but it had better not be rap music. That music is awful, and I can't believe you children actually listen to it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh, please, can we play some rap music? You might like it, Mom.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Well, only if you promise that there is no bad language in it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: There isn't any bad language, I promise!

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: All right, I'll play the CD, but it will be at the volume I choose.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Thanks, Mom.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Have I ever told you about the songs I liked at your age? People listened to real music in those days.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Oh, Mom! Rap is real music, too!

lessons.title: The Report
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 23 The Report.mp3

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I finished my report on the French Revolution last night.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: How did you finish it so fast? I'm still trying to find books about it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: There was something about the French Revolution on TV last week. I wrote down the names of all the people who were on the show.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: What did you do next?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I went to the library and looked for their books. It was very easy, especially because I already understood what they wanted to say.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: I guess I could have done that, but I missed the TV show. Why did Ms. Dessard make us write about French history, anyway? She's a French language teacher, not a history teacher.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ms. Dessard said that if we want to understand the language, we should understand the culture. I don't know if I speak better French, but I know more about French history now. If the French Revolution had never happened, French would be a very different language.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: You're right. I'm going to talk to Ms. Dessard now. I'll see you later.

lessons.title: Home Schools
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 24 Home Schools.mp3

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: There are many kinds of schools for many kinds of students. One kind of school is the home school. Home schools are exactly that-schools at home. Parents choose to home school their children for many reasons. Some people feel that public schools are too dangerous. Some people think that the level of education is too low. Some parents do not approve of the subjects their children learn in public schools. If parents choose to home school their children, they must be ready to teach them well. There are many benefits to home schooling. Home schools are very small. There are just one or two students. The student's mother or father is the teacher. Another benefit is that students can study interesting things. Some people think that home schooling is not good for students. They believe public schools teach children discipline. They feel that public schools give a sense of community. In the end, parents must decide if home schooling is the right choice for their children.

lessons.title: Big Brother
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 25 Big Brother.mp3

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: So, how does it feel to have a new baby brother in the house?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's really exciting, but not as easy as I thought it would be, because the baby cries constantly. I love my baby brother, but I don't like all that noise!

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: I know! When my baby sister was born, she cried and slept all the time. I had to help change diapers and feed her.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I hope I never have to change a diaper! My mom and dad do a good job of that. I learned how to heat the bottle to the right temperature, though. Having a new baby around is hard work.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: What do you like most about your new brother?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: He's really cute, and everyone says he looks like me, but with darker hair.

lines.speaker: G
lines.text: Smaller too, of course!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: He laughs when I tickle his little feet. When he grows up a bit, I'll teach him how to ride a bicycle, and we can also play games together! I'm going to be the best big brother in the world! People and Work

lessons.title: The New Boss
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 26 The New Boss.mp3

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: You know, Kim, I think our new boss doesn't like me. I don't understand why.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: That's not true, Trevor! Why, just this morning I heard her say you're a very good employee. She said you work very hard every day.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: That's news to me. I wish she would say it to me, but she just criticizes everything I do.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I think that you're being too sensitive.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Do you really think so? Maybe I just need a vacation. I haven't had one for years.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: It's not good to work so hard, Trevor. I think a vacation is a great idea.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: How about you? Are you happy at work these days?

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Yes, I'm really enjoying working for this new boss. That's why I'm surprised that you think she criticizes your work. Actually, I think she is helping you to improve your work. She's just trying to help.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I didn't realize that. Now that I think about it, you're right. I feel much better.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Good! Let's go for lunch!

lessons.title: The Principal
lessons.localPath: Listening Practice Through Dictation/Listening Practice Through Dictation 2/Audio + Transcipt/Unit 27 The Principal.mp3

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: How long have you been a school principal, Mr. Shin?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: I have been a school principal for 18 years.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: What made you get involved in education?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: When I was 12 years old, I read an article about how the human brain works. I studied very hard. I tried to use my brain well. Soon, I began to get interested in education.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I see!

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: After college, I became a teacher. I was given the position of principal 12 years later.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Do you ever wish that you had done something else?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: When I first started as a principal, I missed being a teacher. I liked spending time with children and helping them learn and grow. However, I knew that I could do a lot of good as a principal.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: You have certainly done a lot of good, Mr. Shin! You started a special program to send all the students in your school to college!
